newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Lack of selling of dlrs keeps Sri Lanka rupee low.
newsitem.headline: Lack of selling of dlrs keeps Sri Lanka rupee low.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed lower as banks held onto dollars in anticipation of further overseas gains by the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.52 to the dollar after opening at 57.47. The rupee closed on Wednesday at 57.33.
"The dollar rose more due to speculation than commercial demand, because banks are betting on the dollar recording more overseas gains," said a Union Bank dealer.
Banks expect the Central Bank to keep pushing up the dollar accordingly, dealers said. The Central Bank has pushed up the U.S. currency by nearly 28 cents in the last 11 market days.
Overnight call rates closed at 13 percent.

"The market is well offered, and should stay so with the recent relaxation of monetary policy," said a Sampath Bank dealer. The Central Bank earlier this month cut statutory reserves by one percentage point to 14, and permitted exporters to borrow in foreign currency.
"Relaxed monetary policy should also cap the Central Bank selling price at a maximum of 58 rupees, in the near future," said the Union Bank dealer.
Central Bank buying and selling prices today were 56.4820 and 57.6230.
